title: Presidential Candidates Fill Thursday with Visits and Interviews
subtitle: Town halls, interviews, and tours of hospitals, shelters, markets, and public works marked Thursday (27)
excerpt: On Thursday (27), presidential candidates took part in town halls, interviews, and visits to hospitals, shelters, markets, workplaces, and public works.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
On Thursday (27), the schedules of the presidential candidates were packed with a series of in-person and media engagements. Key activities included town halls and press interviews, offering contenders the opportunity to present their proposals and answer questions.

Visits to Social Sectors

The candidates also traveled to various sites of public interest. Visited locations included hospitals, where they observed healthcare conditions firsthand; shelters serving vulnerable populations; open-air markets bustling with merchants and consumers; and several workplaces, allowing for direct interaction with workers from different sectors.

Focus on Public Works

In addition to visiting social institutions, their schedules featured activities tied to public works. These actions aim to showcase the candidates' positions on infrastructure and urban development projects, while also allowing the public to closely monitor the progress of construction in their communities.

Combining town halls, interviews, and tours of hospitals, shelters, markets, workplaces, and public works sites, Thursday (27) reflected the wide range of fronts that the presidential candidates are seeking to address in their campaigns.

With information from Agência Brasil.
